summary: The core in williams2.vhd is laid out like the board, not like MAME's Williams-2 driver. Video RAM is six 4-bit-wide RAMs. Their addresses go through the address-decoder PROM, and each nibble has its own write enable. Foreground and background pixels come out of shift registers fed by fetches timed from the H/V counters. Fine X scroll is a pixel delay line, and the background colour bits come straight from vcnt. MAME instead draws a tilemap plus a linear-videoram loop at screen-update time. The blitter steals bus cycles from the halted 6809 on fixed pixel phases, where MAME blits instantly and charges cycles afterwards. The only MAME-flavoured traces are small: a PIA port-A override input that mirrors a MAME device option, and blitter control-bit semantics any correct core has to share.

findings.signal: video RAM addressed through decoder PROM, split into nibble chips
findings.note: The CPU/blitter address goes through a 512x8 PROM (decod_addr -> decod_do). Bits 5:0 become the low RAM address, and bits 7:6 pick one of three banks of separate high and low 4-bit RAMs. MAME treats video RAM as one flat byte array indexed by source[(x/2)*256].

findings.signal: per-nibble write inhibit instead of read-modify-write
findings.note: Blitter transparency and the no-even/no-odd flags drive blit_wr_inh_h/l, which gate the WE of the high or low nibble RAMs. The destination is never read. MAME's blit_pixel reads curpix and merges it with a keepmask in C.

findings.signal: scan-time fetch phases from pixel counter
findings.note: A 6-phase pixel_cnt produces the en_cpu, rom_rd, video_access and graph_access slots. On video_access, 24 bits (6 pixels) from three VRAM banks load the fg shift register. On graph_access, three graphics ROM bytes load the bg shift register. Both shift out 4 bits per pixel, a per-pixel pipeline rather than MAME's tilemap draw followed by a foreground overlay loop.

findings.signal: fine scroll as pixel delay line; coarse scroll added to hcnt
findings.note: The map RAM column is (hcnt+1)+xscroll(10:3), with xscroll(11) XOR-ed into bit 8. The 3 fine bits select a tap of an 11-stage bg_pixels_N delay chain. MAME turns the register into a single pixel scroll offset for its tilemap.

findings.signal: tile flip by address inversion and shift direction
findings.note: Map bit 7 inverts the two column-address bits sent to the graphics ROMs and reverses the bg shift-register direction. MAME sets a TILE_FLIPX flag in a tile_info callback.

findings.signal: palette address built from raster bits and bank latches
findings.note: The palette RAM address is a mux: CPU address, or fg_color_bank & fg pixel when that pixel is non-zero, or else bg_color_bank(5:3) & vcnt(7:5) & bg pixel. The background colour comes from raster counter bits at scan time, not from a per-tile colour code and palette offset.

findings.signal: blitter as cycle-stealing DMA with HALT/BA/BS handshake
findings.note: The blitter raises HALT, takes the bus only when the 6809 reports BA=BS=1, and alternates a read in the graph_access slot with a write in the en_cpu slot. Slow mode toggles blit_go every cycle. MAME runs the whole blit inside control_w and then subtracts an estimated cycle count.

findings.signal: raster counters as preloaded counter chain
findings.note: hcnt wraps at 64 and vcnt reloads to 0x0FC after 0x1FF, giving 260 lines. The PIA interrupt inputs are wired straight to vcnt(5) and a vcnt decode. MAME uses scanline timer callbacks that call cb1_w/ca1_w.

findings.signal: PIA port-A override input mirrors MAME device option
findings.note: The PIA core has an added pa_ddr_ovrd port, and the sound board ties it to x"FF". This is the same behavioural knob MAME sets for this game, rather than modelling the external driver on the port.

findings.signal: end-of-screen line taken from first-gen count240 rather than board's 254
findings.note: PIA1 CA1 is driven by vcnt_240 (vcnt = 0x1F0), which looks like the 'count240' signal of the older Williams driver. MAME's Williams-2 code uses scanline 254. This is a weak sign that the signal was picked by driver analogy.

The register order (cmd, colour, src, dst, width, height), the stride-256 vs stride-1 stepping, and the shift/solid/fg-only bits match MAME, as any working core must. The details differ: width-1 down-counters, no dst X wrap guard, and simpler transparency logic. So this is not a transliteration.
The CB00-CBBF register windows, C980/C984 PIAs, CC00 CMOS, the 0x9000 DMA-inhibit window and page-3 palette selection all match MAME's map, as a correct core must.
